title: Piernik (Polish gingerbread)
hookLine: Polish-inspired piernik (polish gingerbread) with 14 measured ingredients — zero sign-up, instant Cook Mode.

steps.title: Preheat & Prep Your Pan
steps.instructionTemplate: Heat oven to 160C/140C fan/gas 3. Grease and line the base and sides of a deep 20cm cake tin with baking parchment. Put the honey, sugar and butter in a medium saucepan and cook over a medium heat until fully melted. Remove from the heat and allow to cool. Put the flour and spices in a large bowl and mix everything together. Incorporate {m53292_1}, {m53292_2}, {m53292_3}, and {m53292_4} smoothly until evenly distributed.
steps.creatorSecret: Prep and measure unsalted butter first—mise en place makes this dessert twice as fast.

steps.title: Sift & Whisk Dry Ingredients
steps.instructionTemplate: Once the liquid ingredients have cooled, whisk in the eggs. Pour over the dry ingredients, whisking them together to form a smooth batter – be careful not to overmix as this can lead to a dry cake. Pour into the prepared tin and bake for 50-55 mins or until risen and a skewer inserted into the middle of the cake comes out clean. Allow the cake to cool in the pan for 20 mins before turning out onto a wire rack to cool completely. Incorporate {m53292_5}, {m53292_6}, {m53292_7}, {m53292_8}, {m53292_9}, {m53292_10}, {m53292_11}, {m53292_12}, {m53292_13}, and {m53292_14} smoothly until evenly distributed.

steps.title: Bake Piernik (Polish gingerbread) & Check Doneness
steps.instructionTemplate: Bake for 30 minutes until the edges turn golden and set while the center remains tender. Test with a toothpick—if it comes out with a few moist crumbs rather than wet batter, it is ready.

steps.title: Cream Butter & Sugar Fluffy
steps.instructionTemplate: Once cooled, use a large serrated knife to slice the cake into 3 layers. Spread the jam across the 2 bottom cake layers, then reassemble the cake and set aside while you make the glaze. Put the cream, chocolate and honey in a medium pan and cook over a low-medium heat until the chocolate is melted and you have a smooth, pourable mixture. Put the cake on a wire rack set over a parchment-lined baking tray and pour over the glaze, making sure to cover the entire cake. Use a fish slice to carefully transfer the cake to a serving plate and allow the glaze to set. To decorate, dust with a little edible gold powder, if you like. Uniced, this cake will keep for up to 5 days. Once iced, enjoy within 3 days – just keep in the fridge, but remove before serving and eat at room temperature.
steps.criticalTip: Let set for 5–10 minutes before slicing or plating so the textures hold crisp and photogenic!
steps.creatorSecret: Chill the filled crust 10 minutes before baking—cold butter hits the hot oven and puffs into extra-flaky layers.
